cards.explanation: The answer is to come out of her. The LORD says, "Come out of her, My people!" (Jeremiah 51:45). Two things stand out to me here, friends: He calls them "My people," and the word is to leave.
The word is lives. The LORD says, "Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD." (Jeremiah 51:45). Notice the words "…each of you…" He speaks to every one of them.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Do not let your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid when the rumor is heard in the land…" Those rumors are about violence and ruler against ruler (Jeremiah 51:46). Scary news was coming, friends, and I think He wanted their hearts steady before it arrived.

The answer is False. The verse says heaven and earth "…will shout for joy over Babylon…" and it gives the reason: "…because the destroyers from the north will come against her…" (Jeremiah 51:48). This is a heavy passage, but notice that the whole creation is pictured on one side here. The mourning isn't what the verse describes.

The answer is that they died because of Babylon, and this is a heavy line. The verse says Babylon must fall "…on account of the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon." (Jeremiah 51:49). It puts the two groups side by side, friends. Babylon's fall is tied to the ones who fell because of her.

The answer is the LORD and Jerusalem. The verse says, "Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind." (Jeremiah 51:50). Notice the order, bakers, with the LORD first. Even from far away, their minds are told where to turn.

The answer is that foreigners entered the LORD's holy places. The speakers say, "disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house." (Jeremiah 51:51). I think this one hurts, and the verse says it plainly. The reason is right there in the text.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers I send will come against her…" (Jeremiah 51:53). Babylon can climb as high as she wants, friends, and fortify her stronghold. The destroyers He sends still come against her.

The answer is that He will silence it. The verse says, "For the LORD will destroy Babylon; He will silence her mighty voice." (Jeremiah 51:55). Notice it's not her little voice, friends, it's her MIGHTY one. Loudest one in the room, and now not a peep.
The answer is that He will repay in full. The verse says, "…the LORD is a God of retribution; He will repay in full." (Jeremiah 51:56). Notice "in full," friends. Nothing is left half done.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up…" declares the King (Jeremiah 51:57). It's a heavy word, so I'll say it plainly, friends. There's no waking up the next morning.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts. The verse says, "declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts." (Jeremiah 51:57). The word about Babylon's leaders comes from the King Himself, bakers. He gives His own name right there.

The answer is that her high gates will be consumed by fire. The LORD of Hosts says, "Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire." (Jeremiah 51:58). Thick walls and high gates are the parts a city leans on, friends, and both get named here. I think that's a lot of building to see go.

The answer is False. The LORD of Hosts says, "So the labor of the people will be for nothing; the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames." (Jeremiah 51:58). All that effort doesn't last, friends. It just feeds the fire.
